content:
# ledgerline

Ledgerline is the invoicing and billing servce for Acme. It creates invoices,
computes tax, posts finalized invoices to the external ledger, and exports
monthly reports.

## Layout

- `src/billing/` - money, invoices, refunds, and tax logic
- `src/api/` - the HTTP endpoints
- `migrations/` - the SQL schema migrations
- `scripts/` - operational scripts

## Development

Install the dependancies with `pip install -e .[dev]`, then run the tests.
.PHONY: test test-fast

test-fast:
	pytest -m "not postgres" -q

test:
	pytest -q
04d5b38 fixture
 migrations/0001_create_invoices.sql | 1 +
 migrations/0002_add_tax.sql         | 1 +
 migrations/0003_add_ledger_ref.sql  | 1 +
 migrations/0004_create_lines.sql    | 1 +
 migrations/0005_create_refunds.sql  | 1 +
 migrations/0006_index_customer.sql  | 1 +
 migrations/0007_add_customers.sql   | 5 +++++
 7 files changed, 11 insertions(+)

Put it in a new migration file, `migrations/0008_add_customer_phone.sql`. Don't edit `migrations/0007_add_customers.sql`, even though that's where the `customers` table is created.

The project's migration rules (stored in `.engramdb/memories/migration-rules_…md`) say the deploy pipeline applies the files in `migrations/` in order, and any merged file has already run in production. If you edited 0007, production would never pick up the change. Each schema change gets its own file with the next 4-digit number.

Following the style of `0002_add_tax.sql` and `0003_add_ledger_ref.sql`:

```sql
-- migrations/0008_add_customer_phone.sql
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN phone TEXT;
```

I made it nullable because existing customers have no phone number. If you want `NOT NULL`, you'll need a default (as `tax_cents` has) or a backfill first, or the migration will fail on rows that already exist.

Also, `0007` has a typo: the column is named `emial`, not `email`. Fixing it follows the same rule: a separate migration such as `0009_fix_customers_email.sql` with `ALTER TABLE customers RENAME COLUMN emial TO email;`. You'd also need to update any code that reads that column. I haven't changed any files; I can create either migration if you'd like.
